30. Para No.13 of Plaint is as under:
The plaintiff submits that, as explained above as to the filing of the suit in O.S. No.
7260/2005 and in terms of the Compromise Petition, all the other terms and conditions of three registered lease deeds, dated 26.3.1998, 28.3.1998 and 31.3.1998 and Supplement Agreement, dated 6.11.1998 shall remain unaltered and there are binding on both the parties viz., the plaintiff and the defendants 1 to 4.

The plaintiff submits that, conjoint reading of clause 5 of the registered lease deeds, dated 26.3.1998, 28.3.1998 and 31.3.1998 that, "the payment of monthly rent on or before the dates stipulated above is the essence of this lease deed and under no circumstances, there shall be any delay in payment of the same.

In the event of delay in payment of monthly rents on or before the stipulated dates referred above and such arrears exceed rent for two months, the Lessee shall pay the Lessor interest at 18% pa on the unpaid rents and the Lessee agrees for the same and further in the event of default in payment of rents by the Lessee for any two consecutive months and 60 days notice to that effect, the Lessor shall in addition to claiming of rents with interest, be entitled to terminate the lease without waiting for the expiry of the un-expiry period of lease or renewed period and recover possession of the Schedule property at the cost of the Lessee".

In terms of clause- 5 of lease deed, the stipulated period for payment of monthly rents is on or before 10th day of every English calendar month and even as per he compromise petition filed in O.S.7260/2005, the said terms have not been altered, as such though the matter has been compromised in O.S.No.4022/2017 terms of the compromise decree drawn in O.S. No. 7260/2005,
the plaintiff has a right to terminate the Tenancy, as and when the 1st defendant commits default in paying monthly rents for two months continuously."
31.

Combined reading of lease deed, compromise petition filed in O.S.7260/2005, averments of wriitten statement of defendants No.1 makes it clear that there is default in payment of rent by defendants No.1 and 2 notwithstanding the agreed period of lease in Ex.P1 to P4, plaintiff has a right to terminate the tenancy.
Hence, termination notice dated 12.4.2017 at Ex.P9 issued by plaintiff to defendant is perfectly valid and legal.
Legal notice at Ex.P9 was duly served upon defendants, they have to meet the legal demand made therein.
Thus this suit is maintainable as well.
Hence, I answer issue Nos.1 & 3 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Thus, it is clear admission on the part of defendants No.1 and 2 that the rents for the month of February 2017 and March 2017 has not been paid by defendants.
Hence, I answer issue No.2 in the affirmative.
35. Issue No.4:
In the suit three prayers are sought for, prayer (a) is for direction to defendant to quit and deliver the vacant possession of the suit schedule property to the plaintiff with costs.

While answering issue Nos. 1 and 2, it has been discussed that the tenancy of defendants has been duly terminated and the default in payment of rent committed by defendants has necessitated issuance of notice for termination of tenancy.

Defendants being in possession of suit schedule property are the best persons to know and to ascertain as to what extent of suit schedule property was acquired by KIADB, it is specific contention of defendant in para No.13 of written statement that they approached the plaintiff for determination of rent payable for existing premises after acquisition by KIADB.

Along with written statement, defendants produced O.S.No.4022/2017 documents issued by the Land Acquisition Officer, KIADB which demonstrates that portion of suit schedule property has been acquired by KIADB and compensation has been paid by KIADB to plaintiff.
The remaining extent of suit schedule property in terms of sq.ft or in terms of any other measurement is not at all stated by defendants in their written statement.
It is common knowledge that the rate of rent payable would always depend on extent of leased premises.
Defendants have pleaded and produced documents to the effect that certain portion of suit schedule property was acquired by KIADB.

This being the situation, defendant was duty bound to calculate the pro-rota rent payable taking the rent that was paid by defendants for the month of January 2017 as the basis, which they have failed to do so.

36. Even plaintiff has not produced any documents to substantiate that after termination of tenancy,
defendant is liable to pay damages, in excess of rent that was paid for the month of January 2017.
Further, in plaint, there is no prayer for recovery of arrears of rent and also pend lite damages from defendant.

However, prayer to order for enquiry into mesne profits u/O XX Rule 12 from the date of suit is sought for, considering the factual circumstance plaintiff is entitled to relief sought for in the suit.
Hence, it is hereby ordered that there shall be a separate enquiry for mesne profits.
Hence, I answer issue No.4 partly in the affirmative.
37. Issue No.5:

In view of the findings on issue No.1 to 4, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Suit of the plaintiff is hereby decreed in part with costs.
Defendants No.1 to 4 are hereby directed to quit, vacate and deliver possession of the entire remaining extent of suit schedule property after acquisition by KIADB to plaintiff within 3 months.
